questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to manipulate a 128-bit value using two 64-bit parts and leverage available intrinsics for performance. It tests understanding of bit significance ordering and boundary cases (zero input).

## Key Concepts

- 128-bit represented as two 64-bit words (lo then hi) and how trailing zeros map across the boundary
- Using 64-bit ctz intrinsics to build a 128-bit result in constant time
- Correct handling of the all-zero input returning 128

## Code Example

```c
int trailingZeroCount128(uint128 x) {
  if (x.lo != 0) return __builtin_ctzll(x.lo);
  if (x.hi != 0) return 64 + __builtin_ctzll(x.hi);
  return 128;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you implement this without compiler intrinsics?
- How would you port the approach to a 256-bit representation?
